subject: Geography
description: Cropping seasons, major crops, growing regions, agri policies

questions.stem: KHARIF CROPS in India are sown around:

options.option_text: Monsoon arrival (June-July) + harvested Sep-Oct
Winter (October-November) and harvested March-April
Pre-summer (March-April) and harvested July-August
Year-round, irrigation-dependent farming

questions.explanation: KHARIF (मानसूनी / monsoon) crops — sown JUNE-JULY (with SW monsoon onset), harvested SEP-OCT. Need warm + wet conditions. KEY KHARIF CROPS: rice (paddy), maize, jowar, bajra, ragi, cotton, jute, sugarcane, soybean, groundnut, pulses (arhar/tur, moong, urad). RABI crops — sown OCT-NOV, harvested MAR-APR. Need cool + dry conditions. KEY RABI CROPS: WHEAT (largest), barley, mustard, peas, gram (chana), masoor, linseed, oats. ZAID — short summer crops (March-June); watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables, fodder. Indian agri = ~50% of workforce, ~17% of GDP. NORTHERN states (Punjab, Haryana, UP) — wheat-rice belt. SOUTHERN: rice + cotton + spices. EAST: rice + jute. MONSOON dependence is a key vulnerability.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: India's LARGEST PRODUCER of WHEAT is:

options.option_text: Uttar Pradesh (largest wheat producer)
Punjab (highest yield per hectare)
Madhya Pradesh (rapid riser)
Haryana (early Green Revolution)

questions.explanation: WHEAT PRODUCTION: UP (largest, ~30%), then Punjab + Haryana + MP. UP has largest TOTAL output due to size + Indo-Gangetic plain fertility. PUNJAB has HIGHEST YIELD per hectare ('granary of India'). Indian wheat output ~110 MT (FY24). India world's 2nd largest wheat producer (after CHINA, ~140 MT). RICE: largest = West Bengal, then UP, Punjab, Telangana. India world's 2nd largest rice producer (after CHINA), but LARGEST EXPORTER. SUGARCANE: UP largest, then Maharashtra. COTTON: Gujarat, Maharashtra. PULSES: MP largest. TEA: Assam (50%). COFFEE: Karnataka. SPICES: Kerala (cardamom), Andhra (chilli), Gujarat (cumin), Tamil Nadu (turmeric). ICAR — Indian Council of Agricultural Research, oversees research, sets standards.

questions.stem: India is world's LARGEST PRODUCER of which agricultural commodity?

options.option_text: Milk + jute + pulses + spices (multiple firsts)
Wheat (No. 2; China is No. 1) too alone
Cotton (close, but China leads) too
Rice (No. 2; China is No. 1) too alone

questions.explanation: INDIA — world's LARGEST producer of: MILK (~22% world share, ~230 MT/year — 'Operation Flood', AMUL); JUTE (~50% world); PULSES (~25%); SPICES (~75%); BANANAS, MANGOES, PAPAYAS; CASTOR; OKRA. India is 2ND in: rice, wheat, sugarcane, groundnut, cotton, FRUITS + VEGETABLES OVERALL (huge variety). Indian milk industry: white revolution (1970-90s) under VERGHESE KURIEN (founder of AMUL) revolutionised dairy — went from milk-deficit to surplus. AMUL = Anand Milk Union Ltd., Anand, Gujarat — world's largest dairy cooperative. NDDB (National Dairy Development Board) = institutional backer. India's per-capita milk consumption: ~440 g/day; rising over time. Globally: India ranks #1 in MILK above USA, China, Pakistan.

questions.stem: MSP (Minimum Support Price) is announced by:

options.option_text: CACP (Commission for Agricultural Costs + Prices)
RBI (regulator of banks alone) too alone
FCI (Food Corp of India only buyer) too
NABARD (rural development bank) too alone

questions.explanation: MSP — recommended by CACP (Commission for Agricultural Costs + Prices, attached to Min of Agri) → approved by CABINET COMMITTEE ON ECONOMIC AFFAIRS (CCEA). FCI (Food Corp of India) + state agencies BUY at MSP from farmers. Currently MSP for ~23 CROPS. KEY: WHEAT, RICE, BAJRA, JOWAR, MAIZE, TUR, MOONG, URAD, COTTON, MUSTARD, GROUNDNUT, SOYBEAN, SUNFLOWER, SUGARCANE (FRP, separate). MSP CALCULATION: A2 (cash costs); A2+FL (cash + family labour); C2 (full cost incl. land rent + capital interest). MSP currently = A2+FL × 1.5 (since 2018). DEMAND for legal MSP guarantee = key to farmer protests (esp. 2020-21). CONTROVERSY: only ~6% of farmers benefit (mostly Punjab/Haryana wheat-rice); rest face mandi prices.

questions.stem: TROPICAL CROP grown mainly in COASTAL STATES of India is:

options.option_text: Coconut (Kerala, TN, Karnataka, Andhra)
Wheat (Punjab + Haryana + UP)
Apples (Himachal + Kashmir) too
Saffron (Kashmir's Pampore area)

questions.explanation: COCONUT — needs warm + humid + saline coastal climate. India's main coconut states: KERALA ('Kera' = coconut tree in Malayalam — state's name itself; ~37% national output), TAMIL NADU, KARNATAKA, ANDHRA PRADESH, ANDAMAN-NICOBAR. India is world's 3RD largest coconut producer (after Indonesia + Philippines). USES: copra, oil, water, fibre (coir, ropes, mats), shell. KERALA STATE TREE — coconut. KERALA also: spice exports (cardamom — 'queen of spices'; pepper — 'king'; cinnamon, clove). Compare: APPLES — temperate climate, HIMACHAL + J&K. SAFFRON — Kashmir (PAMPORE), only in India's Karewas (mid-altitude shelves) — world's most expensive spice (~₹2-3 lakh/kg).

questions.stem: BLACK SOIL (regur soil) is most suitable for which crop?

options.option_text: Cotton (regur = 'black cotton soil')
Tea (laterite + acidic soil)
Apples (alluvial mountain soil)
Coffee (laterite, Western Ghats)

questions.explanation: BLACK SOIL (REGUR) — formed from BASALTIC LAVA (Deccan trap area). Found in: MAHARASHTRA, GUJARAT, MADHYA PRADESH, parts of Karnataka + Andhra. RICH in calcium, magnesium, iron, potash; LOW in nitrogen + phosphorus. RETAINS MOISTURE well — good for DRY CROPS, esp. COTTON ('black cotton soil'). Also good for soybean, sugarcane, sorghum, pulses. EXPANDS when wet, CRACKS when dry → 'self-ploughing' soil. INDIAN SOIL TYPES: ALLUVIAL (most fertile, Indo-Gangetic plains, ~40% area; rice + wheat + sugarcane); BLACK / Regur; RED + YELLOW (Deccan plateau, less fertile; millets, pulses); LATERITE (heavy rain areas, SW + E coasts; tea, coffee, rubber, cashew); ARID (Rajasthan, low organic; bajra, drought-resistant); MOUNTAIN; PEATY + SALINE.

questions.stem: ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research) headquarters is at:

options.option_text: New Delhi (Pusa campus)
Mumbai (financial capital)
Bengaluru (tech capital)
Hyderabad (CCMB area)

questions.explanation: ICAR — headquartered in NEW DELHI (Pusa campus, Krishi Bhavan). FOUNDED 1929 as Imperial Council of Agri Research; renamed 1946. Apex body for coordinating agricultural research + education in India. RUNS 100+ INSTITUTES + RESEARCH CENTRES across India. Key ones: IARI (Indian Agricultural Research Institute, Pusa, New Delhi — wheat varieties, GR development); IRRI (International Rice Research Institute, Philippines — Indian collaboration); NDRI (Karnal — dairy); IISR (Lucknow — sugarcane); CICR (Nagpur — cotton); IIVR (Varanasi — vegetables); CIFE (Mumbai — fisheries education); KVK (Krishi Vigyan Kendras) — district-level extension. NORMAN BORLAUG visited IARI; gave dwarf wheat. MS SWAMINATHAN was DG of ICAR (1972-79) + later Min of Agri's advisor + Rajya Sabha MP (2007).

questions.stem: Which of the following crops belongs to the RABI season in India?

options.option_text: Groundnut — an oilseed cultivated in the Kharif season
Mustard — an oilseed sown in winter and harvested in spring
Soybean — a legume crop grown mainly in the Kharif season
Cotton — a fibre crop that belongs to the Kharif category

questions.explanation: Mustard is a classic Rabi crop sown in October–November (post-monsoon) and harvested in March–April. Groundnut, soybean, and cotton are all Kharif crops sown during the June–July monsoon onset. The common trap is confusing groundnut (oilseed like mustard) as Rabi — but groundnut thrives in warm, moist conditions of the Kharif season.

questions.stem: The term 'WHITE REVOLUTION' in Indian agriculture refers to the increase in production of which commodity?

options.option_text: Sugar — expanded through cooperative mills of western Maharashtra
Wheat — introduction of high-yielding semi-dwarf Mexican varieties
Milk — national cooperative dairy development programme
Cotton — mechanised ginning and pressing drive of the 1970s

questions.explanation: White Revolution refers to Operation Flood (launched 1970) under Dr. Verghese Kurien through NDDB, which transformed India into the world's largest milk producer via cooperative dairies. The common confusion is with 'Green Revolution' (wheat/rice HYV seeds). Sugar has no named revolution; cotton is sometimes called 'White Gold' but that is a price-based term, not a revolution.

questions.stem: Which Indian state accounts for the LARGEST AREA under sugarcane cultivation?

options.option_text: Maharashtra — the sugar cooperative belt of western districts
Uttar Pradesh — the Ganga-Yamuna Doab and Tarai cane belt
Karnataka — the Krishna basin irrigated sugarcane zone
Tamil Nadu — the Cauvery delta sugarcane-growing tracts

questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh commands roughly 50% of India's total sugarcane area, with the Ganga–Yamuna Doab and the Tarai belt being dominant. Maharashtra is a common wrong answer because it leads in sugar recovery (yield per hectare) and sugar production value — but area-wise, UP dominates. Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are significant but distant third and fourth.

questions.stem: The Geographical Indication (GI) tag for 'Alphonso (Hapus) Mango' is registered to which producing region?

options.option_text: Talala sub-district of Gir-Somnath district in Gujarat
Konkan coast districts of Maharashtra — Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg
Krishnapatnam and Nellore coastal belt of Andhra Pradesh
Malihabad tehsil of Lucknow district in Uttar Pradesh

questions.explanation: Alphonso (Hapus) mango GI tag covers Konkan districts of Maharashtra including Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg, Raigad, Thane, and Palghar. Option A (Gir-Somnath, Gujarat) is the GI region for Kesar mango — a very frequent mix-up in exams. Option D (Malihabad, UP) is associated with the Dussehri mango variety.

questions.stem: Jute is called the 'GOLDEN FIBRE' of India. Which statement about India's jute industry is CORRECT?

options.option_text: India is the world's largest jute producer, ahead of Bangladesh
India ranks second in jute production globally, after Bangladesh
India exports raw jute but imports all finished jute products
West Bengal and Assam together account for less than 40% of Indian jute area

questions.explanation: India is the world's second-largest jute producer after Bangladesh, though India is the largest consumer and processor of jute. West Bengal alone accounts for over 50% of India's jute cultivation (Assam adds another ~8%), making Option D wrong. Option A reverses the global rank — a classic exam trap. Jute is called 'Golden Fibre' for its golden-brown sheen and economic value in packaging.

questions.stem: Under PM-KISAN (PM Kisan Samman Nidhi), the ₹6,000 annual income support to eligible farmer families is disbursed in how many instalments and of what amount each?

options.option_text: Two equal tranches of ₹3,000 each at sowing season intervals
Three equal instalments of ₹2,000 each, every four months
Four quarterly instalments of ₹1,500 each throughout the year
One annual lump-sum transfer of ₹6,000 after the Rabi harvest

questions.explanation: PM-KISAN (launched Feb 2019) disburses ₹6,000/year in three instalments of ₹2,000 each covering windows: April–July, August–November, and December–March. Option C (quarterly = 4 instalments) is the most common wrong answer since quarterly sounds administratively natural. A lump-sum transfer (Option D) was never the design — timely instalments support both Kharif and Rabi input costs.

questions.stem: Which of the following CORRECTLY pairs a GI-tagged Indian crop variety with its registered producing state?

options.option_text: Kesar Mango → Gujarat; Navara Rice → Tamil Nadu
Kesar Mango → Gujarat; Navara Rice → Kerala
Kesar Mango → Maharashtra; Navara Rice → Kerala
Kesar Mango → Gujarat; Navara Rice → West Bengal

questions.explanation: Kesar mango GI tag belongs to Gir-Somnath district, Gujarat — its arid-to-semi-arid climate gives the variety its distinctive saffron colour and aroma. Navara rice is an ancient, short-grained medicinal rice variety from Kerala, used in Ayurvedic treatments, holding a GI tag from Kerala. Tamil Nadu (Option A) is a frequent distractor for Navara because of its rice-farming prominence; Maharashtra (Option C) is confused with Kesar due to its Alphonso fame.
